A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CP-Trie evaluation framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CP-Trie experiments across seven language models and repeated TruthfulQA evaluations, with detailed results in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original Llama-2-7B evaluations on MBPP, HumanEval and GSM8K in Section 6.

M1.justification: The CP-Trie construction, token-count recall/risk measures and comparison at fixed average risks remain substantively unchanged. Explicit averaging formulas and newly documented tokenization handling do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds code generation on MBPP and HumanEval and mathematical problem solving on GSM8K, substantially extending coverage beyond the retained English Wikipedia CP-Trie and TruthfulQA evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new benchmarks reuse Top-k, Top-p, Mirostat, eta sampling and greedy decoding, all previously evaluated. Min-P and Locally Typical Sampling are discussed as omissions, not added comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 adds Llama-2-7B evaluations following Shi et al.'s setup, using Pass@1 for coding and accuracy for GSM8K at average risks 1, 5 and 15. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged; the added tokenization and grid-search descriptions document previously unspecified details.

E4.justification: v1 Figure 7's two-question greedy-decoding case study is removed. The model-size analysis, entropy/truncation correlations and probability-distribution examples remain; the entropy analysis moves to v2 Appendix A.1 rather than being deleted.

E5.justification: Both versions report three TruthfulQA runs with means and standard deviations, plus CP-Trie risk/recall standard errors. The new benchmark tables follow the existing three-run mean/standard-deviation practice. The explicit RSE formula clarifies an already reported statistic.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 add substantial coding and mathematics results. For example, HumanEval reports eta sampling at 6.91 versus greedy decoding at 2.44, while MBPP reports greedy decoding at 24.00 above every sampler. These are new comparisons, not same-setting performance improvements. The earlier main and appendix numerical tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v2 removes the sequence-error accumulation equation from v1 Section 3.2 and the entire low-variance risk conjecture with its AM-GM argument from Section 4.3. Neither is relocated to the appendix, substantially reducing the theoretical justification connecting per-step stability to sequence-level risk. The basic support, recall and risk definitions remain.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit contribution claiming that existing evaluation underestimates sampling methods because of parameter-selection difficulties. The central claims about CP-Trie evaluation and practical sampling-parameter guidance remain.

C2.justification: v2 tentatively attributes Mirostat's weak coding/math performance to its natural-language Zipf-law basis and acknowledges a HumanEval greedy-baseline discrepancy. It replaces v1's asserted cross-language transferability with future dataset extension and explicitly acknowledges omitted sampling methods.

D1.justification: v2 supplies important previously missing reproduction information: word/subtoken matching, skipped continuation subtokens, a 2,000-point coarse-to-fine search, a ±0.1 risk tolerance and grids determined using Llama-3-70B. It also adds a code-repository link and states that the benchmark is public. These are documentation/access additions, not evidence of rerunning existing experiments.

R1.justification: Shi et al. changes from a surveyed evaluation study into the target of a dedicated empirical reassessment and a highlighted contribution claiming underestimated sampling performance. This substantially strengthens the paper's positioning against prior evaluation practice. Austin et al., Finlayson et al. and Nguyen et al. are also newly cited.

P1.justification: The abstract and several explanatory passages are tightened, AR/RSE terminology is standardized, and 'parameter-independent' becomes 'tuning-independent.' Construction details move from the introduction to data collection, entropy discussion moves to the appendix, and affiliations are updated. Much of the retained exposition remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds three benchmark tables, removes the greedy-example figure, relocates and enlarges the entropy plots, and reformats the appendices into full-width presentation. Table 1 reorders methods and replaces blue worst-score highlighting with underlining. These changes substantially reorganize the displays.

improvement.justification: The coding/math evaluations provide useful evidence about task-dependent behavior, while the tokenization, search and access details improve reproducibility. Revised limitations also avoid v1's unsupported cross-language generalization. The gains remain bounded by the acknowledged HumanEval baseline discrepancy and removal of the sequence-risk theoretical rationale, supporting a limited overall improvement.
